meta.note: Tuesday briefing. Three top stories: the aluminum squeeze expires tomorrow (spot premium widened to USD 275/ton on Nov 16, a 36-year high); copper LME 3M hit a 4-month low while SHFE spot premiums and the Yangshan premium both hit record highs; NVIDIA reports after the close tonight plus the U.S. Nov 16 new chip export controls, with the stock down about 36% from its October high. Industry updates: Modine renamed Modexus Solutions, Vertiv ATLAS Lab, Midea R290, tariff check found no new finalized measures. Events library: 4 new events created (gallium/germanium/antimony pause expiry, Vertiv ATLAS Lab, ABB robotics sale blocked, Schneider's PTC acquisition vote), 10 timeline entries added. hotspot_events.title: Aluminum squeeze expires tomorrow; spot premium hits another 36-year high
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Spot premium of USD 275/ton, a fresh 36-year high; November contract open interest exceeds total exchange inventory, LME stocks at their lowest since 1990, and delivery on Nov 18 is imminent — aluminum fin and profile costs and lead times are under pressure in parallel
hotspot_events.summary: LME 3M was about USD 3,010–3,019/ton on Nov 16; the spot premium over 3M widened to USD 275/ton on Nov 16, far above the Nov 12 intraday high of USD 176.80/ton, with Reuters calling the tightness unseen since the twin squeezes of 1988 and 1990; LME inventories stood at 224,150 tons (Nov 13, the lowest since 1990), 99.98% of Russian origin, with a single holder accounting for 30–39% of warrants; aggregate November contract open interest exceeds total exchange inventory, and four undisclosed longs together hold at least 25% of open interest; the November contract expires Nov 18 (Wednesday), and as of Nov 16 there was no new notice of the LME triggering forced-lending rules or emergency intervention.

hotspot_events.title: NVIDIA reports after the close tonight plus U.S. Nov 16 new chip export controls
hotspot_events.heat_reason: The first earnings report since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO lands after the close tonight, with the stock down about 36% from its October high, compounded by the U.S. Nov 16 new chip export controls closing the remote-computing loophole — sentiment and order pacing across the AI infrastructure chain face repricing
hotspot_events.summary: NVIDIA reports FY2027 Q3 results after the U.S. market close on Nov 17 (earnings call 17:00 ET); consensus expects revenue of about USD 109.2 billion and adjusted EPS of about USD 2.47–2.48, with data-center revenue expected at about USD 101.8 billion (which would mark the first quarter above USD 100 billion); the company guided revenue of USD 108 billion (±2%) and gross margin of 74.0% (±0.5pp), and management has already flagged Q4 gross margin dipping to 71%–72%; NVDA closed at USD 156.14 on Nov 16 (-4.12%), down about 35.9% from its 52-week high of USD 243.37 (Oct 6); the U.S. Commerce Department's BIS issued an interim final rule on Nov 16 requiring licenses for exports of advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, and closing the loophole under which Chinese companies remotely rented computing power via third-country data centers (the remote-computing clause takes effect in 90 days); the board has not discussed bringing Jensen Huang back (CNBC, Nov 16).
numbers: Consensus expects revenue of about USD 109.2 billion, adjusted EPS of about USD 2.47–2.48
Data-center revenue expected at about USD 101.8 billion (first quarter above USD 100 billion)

industry_updates.title: Modine renamed Modexus Solutions as Nov 18 Investor Day approaches
industry_updates.detail: Modine announced on Nov 16 that shareholders voted in favor and the company has formally been renamed Modexus Solutions (ticker remains MOD); an analyst and investor day will be held in Chicago at 10:00 ET on Nov 18 (Wednesday), updating its multi-year growth strategy and new financial targets; FY2027 guidance: continuing-operations revenue of USD 3.1–3.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA of USD 470–500 million, and data-center revenue +80–90%; Samsung acquisition talks remained unconfirmed by either side as of Nov 16, with no offer disclosed; Modine closed at USD 135.66 on Nov 13 (+27.86%), up a cumulative +40.42% for the week.

industry_updates.title: Vertiv ATLAS Lab now in service
industry_updates.detail: Vertiv announced on Nov 16 that its ATLAS Lab in Columbus, Ohio is now in service, conducting system-level validation of power, cooling and controls for AI factories before chips reach the market, aiming to shorten customer deployment cycles; its engineering collaboration with NVIDIA covers modeling, power architecture, liquid cooling and controls; no revenue or order figures were disclosed.

industry_updates.title: Midea R290 technology showcased at MOP38
industry_updates.detail: Midea's residential air-conditioning unit attended the MOP38 Innovation Exhibition in Montreal on Nov 2–6, showcasing R290 air-conditioning technology with refrigerant charge reduced by up to 40% versus conventional solutions (at equal cooling capacity and efficiency); according to Euromonitor, Midea has been the world's No. 1 R290 air-conditioner company for four consecutive years.

industry_updates.title: Haier adds UK distributor (minor update)
industry_updates.detail: On Nov 16, Cool Solutions Distribution of Leeds, UK was appointed a Haier HVAC UK distributor, initially focusing on AHU interface solutions, the MRV range and R290 monobloc heat pumps (4–16kW residential, 26–40kW commercial).

industry_updates.title: Tariff policy check: no new finalized measures in the window
industry_updates.detail: The upgraded China–ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 protocol takes effect Dec 1 (general trade facilitation and relaxed rules-of-origin cumulation; no change to HVAC tariff rates); the pause on the gallium/germanium/antimony export ban on the U.S. expires Nov 27, with no extension announced as of Nov 16; the Section 301 exclusion extension to 2027-01-09 and the rare-earth controls pause extension to 2027-01-10 were already reported; the second round of trilateral talks on the CBAM downstream extension is set for Nov 30; the 15% Section 232 tariff on polysilicon takes effect Dec 4; the first China–U.S. Trade Council meeting on Nov 13–14 produced talks only, with no agreement reached, and is not reported under our criteria.
industry_updates.source: Ministry of Commerce Nov 16 briefing via East Asia Brief, 2026-11-16

siphon_effects.detail: NVIDIA reports FY2027 Q3 results after the close on Nov 17; consensus expects revenue of about USD 109.2 billion and adjusted EPS of about USD 2.47–2.48, with data-center revenue expected at about USD 101.8 billion (which would mark the first quarter above USD 100 billion); the Q4 guidance watchpoint is analysts' average expectation of about USD 125 billion in revenue; company guidance already assumes zero data-center computing revenue from China.

Samsung's Q3 results (Nov 16): cumulative Jan–Sep revenue of KRW 500.6261 trillion (+108.8%), operating profit of KRW 254.1657 trillion (about +10.8x), with the DS semiconductor division accounting for 71.2% of revenue and Q3 DRAM market share of 38.3% (+4.3pp); Counterpoint puts Q3 global DRAM revenue up 369% year on year to a record high, with market shares of Samsung 38%, SK Hynix 29% and Micron 21%.

CoreWeave Q3 revenue of USD 3.661 billion (+168% year on year), revenue backlog of USD 132.5 billion (+USD 28.3 billion in the quarter); quarterly capex of USD 14.511 billion and full-year capex guidance of USD 37–39 billion; total debt of USD 46.9 billion; energized power of 1.7GW and contracted power above 4.6GW (only 37% energized); the share price fell -6.13% to USD 53.13 on Nov 13.

Cerebras signed Microsoft (cloud services agreement signed in October, revenue recognition from Q1 2027), its third hyperscaler customer after AWS and Oracle; the reason for the OpenAI 750MW order delivery lag is now confirmed as shortages of land, power and facility buildings (not chips), with the first 250MW due by end-2026 and currently behind schedule; remaining performance obligations of USD 26.1 billion, Q3 core revenue of USD 231 million (+70% year on year), and full-year guidance of USD 940–960 million.

The power bottleneck is escalating: Applied Digital is requiring large tenants such as Oracle and Meta, plus NVIDIA and AMD, to provide billions of dollars in financial guarantees per project to cover grid-upgrade and connection costs for new AI data centers, while explicitly limiting leasing capacity for junk-rated neocloud tenants (naming CoreWeave); global procurement lead times for large power transformers have stretched from about 2 years in 2021 to 160–210 weeks (3–4 years), and Wood Mackenzie expects a 15% power-transformer market shortage in 2026; Siemens Energy's FY2026 backlog is EUR 164 billion, GE Vernova's backlog USD 197 billion, and Eaton's data-center orders have more than doubled on a rolling 12-month basis.

DDRWatcher weekly (updated Nov 16): DDR4 spot average price USD 46.51 (-2.7% week on week, a fourth straight weekly decline), DDR5 USD 60.21 (-1.4%), DDR5 modules USD 243.22 (+0.6%), with market status turning to Correction for the first time in 8 weeks; the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on Nov 14 denied Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron's motion to dismiss the DRAM class action, with the three required to answer by Dec 7; TrendForce said on Nov 6 that DRAM price increases will accelerate further in 2027Q1, with Q4 PC DRAM contract prices up 13%–18% quarter on quarter; Intel's CEO warned on Nov 13 that tight memory supply could persist into 2027.

The U.S. Commerce Department's BIS issued an interim final rule on Nov 16: exports of advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil now require licenses, closing the loophole under which Chinese companies remotely rented computing power via third-country data centers (the remote-computing clause takes effect in 90 days); the rule was drafted under the lead of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council and is the first U.S. policy response since Jensen Huang stepped down; on Nov 16 NVDA fell 4.1%, Micron and Intel fell more than 7%, and AMD fell about 5%.
siphon_effects.source: U.S. Commerce Department BIS via FXStreet, 2026-11-16

cross_industry.detail: Nucor's hot-rolled consumer spot price (CSP) rose another USD 15/short ton on Nov 16 to USD 1,310/short ton (held or raised for 64 consecutive weeks since Aug 25, 2025, a cumulative +USD 435/short ton), with lead times of 3–5 weeks; after plate rose USD 70/short ton on Nov 13, no public follow-on announcements from Cleveland-Cliffs, U.S. Steel, SSAB or others had appeared as of Nov 16; SMU plate average was USD 1,550/short ton as of Nov 10 (+USD 55 week on week) and hot-rolled coil USD 1,375/short ton (+USD 25).

CAAM: October NEV production and sales of 2.017 million and 1.94 million units (+13.8% / +13.1% year on year), with NEVs accounting for 64.3% of new-car sales; October auto exports of 1.066 million units (+60.2% year on year, above 1 million for a fifth straight month), including NEV exports of 606,000 units (+1.4x year on year); cumulative Jan–Oct exports of 9.271 million units (+65.1% year on year), including 4.612 million NEVs (up more than 130% year on year); CAAM expects full-year exports to top 10 million units.
cross_industry.source: CAAM via China Youth Daily Online, 2026-11-13

cross_industry.detail: General Administration of Customs: transformer export value in the first three quarters of 2026 was +22.5% year on year, and wire and cable +28.1%; South Korea's October exports of transformers and static converters were USD 513.6 million (+75.4% year on year), including USD 1.62 billion of large transformers above 10,000kVA over the past 12 months (+34%), with the U.S. accounting for 65.8% of the destination; South Korea's October electrical-equipment exports of USD 1.99 billion (+74.0%) were a monthly record.

N-type dense polysilicon averaged RMB 40.5/kg in the week of Nov 13 (flat week on week), against a production cost of RMB 42.8/kg — a loss of RMB 2.3 per kg; October output was 105,100 tons (-7.81% month on month), with November scheduled output of 82,200 tons (-21.79% month on month) and capacity utilization falling to 28.62%; the U.S. 15% Section 232 tariff on polysilicon takes effect Dec 4.

IDC: Q3 global smartphone shipments of 255.3 million units (-22.0% year on year, the largest single-quarter year-on-year decline on record) and PC shipments of 62.7 million units (-20.1% year on year); IDC says the AI-driven memory crisis has pushed component costs up about 350% since 2025 and still rising, with the constrained market expected to persist into 2027 and recovery earliest in 2028; TrendForce puts notebook CPU+DRAM+SSD at 68% of a USD 900 model's BOM in Q3 2026 (45% in Q1 2025), with server DRAM contract prices up about 270% for full-year 2026.

Indian natural rubber touched a record high of INR 300/kg on Nov 2 (about +62% versus the November 2025 average of INR 186); the Indian Tyre Manufacturers' Association wrote to the Commerce Minister on Nov 6 requesting a temporary duty-free import quota; ANRPC expects 2026 global output of 15.039 million tons versus consumption of 15.356 million tons, a supply gap; no new quotes or official responses within the window.

No new price-increase announcements in the window: Samsung Electro-Mechanics MLCC lead time of 52 weeks (October data, some distributors listing up to 61 weeks), H1 2026 capacity utilization of 91%, and AI-server MLCC long-term contracts of about KRW 2.4 trillion; TrendForce expects the high-end MLCC shortage to extend into H1 2027, with manufacturers opening 2027Q1 price negotiations in November; Yageo's next round of high-capacitance increases of +50% or more remains a brokerage view, unconfirmed; Murata's new capacity can only come online in 2028; KEMET's second round of increases took effect Nov 1 (T520/T521/T530 series +20–30%); industrial-grade aluminum electrolytic capacitors (400–450V) have lead times of 18–22 weeks (iM Securities Oct 21, PCBA-HYH Nov 2)

No new resumption or investigation updates in the window on the Panasonic Hukou (Hsinchu, Taiwan) fire (Nov 5 status: lines still shut down, 2 dead and 5 injured, resumption requiring months or more; the Hukou plant accounts for about 20% of MEGTRON global capacity, equivalent to about 4% of global high-end CCL supply); electronic cloth prices continued to rise in November (Zhuochuang November quotes: 7628 electronic cloth RMB 14.6–14.65/m, +RMB 1.5/m month on month, up more than 250% cumulatively from RMB 4.15/m at end-Q3 2025; 2116 thin cloth RMB 20.2/m, +RMB 2.5/m month on month); Shengyi Technology's November price increase (M6 and below +15%, bonding sheet PP +25%) is an industry-communication view with no official announcement; China Jushi signed a 250-million-meter-per-year electronic cloth project in early November (total investment RMB 2.4 billion) (TrendForce Nov 5, 21st Century Business Herald Nov 3)

DDR4 spot USD 46.51 (-2.7% week on week, a fourth straight weekly decline), DDR5 USD 60.21 (-1.4%), DDR5 modules USD 243.22 (+0.6%); on Nov 14 a U.S. judge denied Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron's motion to dismiss the DRAM antitrust suit (case No. 5:26-cv-06345), with the three required to answer by Dec 7; TrendForce expects Q4 PC DRAM contract prices to rise another 13%–18% quarter on quarter and says price increases will accelerate in 2027Q1; Intel's CEO warned that tight memory supply could persist into 2027 (DDRWatcher Nov 16, TrendForce Nov 6)

ST's fourth price-increase letter of the year (dated Nov 4) says some products will rise from Jan 1, 2027, the fourth such notice in 2026, but the letter lists no specific product lines or increases, and TrendForce noted on Nov 12 that the product scope and increases remain officially unconfirmed, with nothing published on ST's website; Infineon's FY2026 revenue was EUR 16.4 billion (+11.5% year on year), FY2027 guidance about EUR 20 billion, with data-center power business expected at nearly EUR 4 billion; onsemi Q3 revenue was USD 1.722 billion (+11% year on year), AI data-center revenue +175% year on year, about USD 620 million for the full year and expected to double again in 2027 (TrendForce Nov 12, Limchip Nov 11, Infineon results Nov 10, onsemi results Nov 2)

Siemens Digital Industries price adjustment took effect Nov 1 (distributor view: SIMATIC S7-1500 CPUs +15%, S7-1200 G1 +15%, HMI Comfort panels +15%, industrial PCs +25% on average, memory cards +50%/+125%, SINAMICS hardware +9%, with SITOP power supplies included; no press release on Siemens' website); Schneider's Indonesia Digital Energy price factor moved from 1.1 to 1.15 from Nov 1 (about +4.5%, an Indonesia-market notice, not China); ABB will raise prices by an average of +3.2%–5.5% from 2027-02-01 (per a Swiss electrical wholesaler's price-adjustment list); ABB's robotics divestiture was blocked by China (disclosed Nov 5, about USD 5.375 billion), and as of Nov 16 neither side had announced the deal terminated or a restructuring plan; Schneider's PTC acquisition shareholder vote is set for Dec 17 (PLCDCS Tech Nov 4, Schneider Indonesia notice PDF, Swiss Financial Time Nov 13, ad-hoc-news Nov 16)
No new letters in this window (INVT's Oct 8 adjustment and Kehua's Nov 1 adjustment already reported)
